(Atlanta, Georgia) | college = [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]] (2006–2007) | draft_year = 2007 | draft_round = 1 | draft_pick = 19 | draft_team = [[Los Angeles Lakers]] | career_start = 2007 | career_end = 2011 | career_position = [[Point guard]] / [[shooting guard]] | career_number = 1, 3, 8, 23, 6 | years1 = {{nbay|2007|full=y}} | team1 = [[Los Angeles Lakers]] | years2 = {{nbay|2007|end}} | team2 = [[Memphis Grizzlies]] | years3 = {{nbay|2008|full=y}} | team3 = [[Washington Wizards]] | years4 = [[2010–11 CBA season|2010]] | team4 = [[Zhejiang Lions]] | years5 = [[2010–11 NBA Development League season|2011]] | team5 = [[Dakota Wizards]] | highlights = * Third-team [[List of All-Atlantic Coast Conference men's basketball teams|All-ACC]] (2007) * [[Atlantic Coast Conference|ACC]] All-Freshman Team (2007) * [[McDonald's All-American Game|McDonald's All-American]] ([[2006 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2006]]) * Third-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] (2006) * [[Mr. Georgia Basketball]] (2006) | stat1label = [[Point (basketball)|Points]] | stat1value = 595 (5.3 ppg) | stat2label = [[Rebound (basketball)|Rebounds]] | stat2value = 276 (2.4 rpg) | stat3label = [[Assist (basketball)|Assists]] | stat3value = 201 (1.8 apg) }} '''Javaris Cortez Crittenton''' (born December 31, 1987) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player. During his four year career, Crittenton played for the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], [[Memphis Grizzlies]], and [[Washington Wizards]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), the [[Zhejiang Lions]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]], and the [[Dakota Wizards]] of the [[NBA D-League]]. He played college basketball for the [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets]]. On August 26, 2011, Crittenton was charged with the murder of Jullian Jones, a 22-year-old mother of four. After pleading guilty to manslaughter in 2015, he was sentenced to 23 years in prison, though it was later reduced to 10 years. He was released from prison on April 21, 2023. ==Early life== Crittenton was born to Sonya Dixon{{cite web |url=http://ramblinwreck.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/crittenton_javaris00.html |title=Player Bio: Javaris Crittenton |work=RamblinWreck.com |publisher=Georgia Tech Athletic Association |access-date=June 29, 2007 |archive-date=July 6, 2007 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070706082127/http://ramblinwreck.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/crittenton_javaris00.html |url-status=dead }} in [[Atlanta]], [[Georgia (U.S. state)|Georgia]].[https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/3197/javaris-crittenton Javaris Crittendon], espn.com, accessed February 13, 2007. He attended [[Southwest Atlanta Christian Academy]], where, as a high school [[tenth grade|sophomore]], he played alongside [[Dwight Howard]], who was a [[twelfth grade|senior]] at the time. Crittenton and Howard led Southwest Atlanta to victory in the [[Georgia High School Association|GHSA]] class A state championship that season. As a [[eleventh grade|junior]], in 2005, Crittenton averaged 28.4 [[point (basketball)|points]], 7.5 [[assist (basketball)|assists]], and 8.2 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]]. He once again led Southwest Atlanta to the GHSA class A state finals, where they lost to powerhouse Randolph-Clay. As a [[twelfth grade|senior]], Crittenton averaged 29 points, 9 assists and 7 rebounds, and led Southwest Atlanta to the GHSA class A semi-finals against Randolph-Clay. After dismissing Randolph-Clay they headed to the championship game once again. This time they were successful in beating rivals Whitefield Academy to become state champions. Following the season he was named a [[McDonald's All American]]. He was also named Mr. Georgia Basketball by ''[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]''. Crittenton carried a 3.5 [[Grading in education#United States|GPA]] in high school, and was a member of the [[FBLA|Future Business Leaders of America]] and the Senior Beta Club. ==College career== [[File:Javaris Crittenton (cropped).jpg|thumb|right|Crittenton with the [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets]] in 2006]] While at Georgia Tech, Crittenton excelled and was considered a team leader, a rare accolade for a freshman.{{cite news |last=Odum |first=Charles |title=College Basketball: Georgia Tech 74, N.C. State 65 |url=http://www.salisburypost.com/Sports/ncsta |work=Salisbury Post |agency=Associated Press |date=February 7, 2007 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121007121515/http://www.salisburypost.com/Sports/ncsta |archive-date=October 7, 2012 |df=mdy-all }} Tech coach [[Paul Hewitt]] urged Crittenton to take over a leadership role on the team after his play in several games in February 2007. He recorded a career high of 29 points in a February 13 game against [[Florida State Seminoles|Florida State]].Associated Press. [https://web.archive.org/web/20110525010619/http://sports.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=270440052 Georgia Tech 63, Florida St 57], espn.com, accessed March 11, 2007. After a single season, he left school to go pro. ==Professional career== === Los Angeles Lakers (2007–2008) === Crittenton was drafted with the 19th pick in the first round of the [[2007 NBA draft]] by the Los Angeles Lakers. During an [[NBA]] Summer League game on July 8, 2007, he had 18 points, including a game winning jump-shot with 1.6 seconds left in the game. In the Lakers' first preseason game against the [[Golden State Warriors]] in [[Honolulu]], Crittenton had 18 points along with one assist in a 111–110 loss. ===Memphis Grizzlies (2008)=== On February 1, 2008, Crittenton was traded to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] along with [[Kwame Brown]], [[Aaron McKie]], rights to [[Marc Gasol]] and [[2008 NBA Draft|2008]] and [[2010 NBA Draft|2010]] first round draft picks for [[Pau Gasol]] and a [[2010 NBA Draft|2010]] second round draft pick.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/grizzlies/news/grizzlies_trade_gasol_to_lakers-080201.html |title=Grizzlies trade Pau Gasol to Lakers for four players and two first-round picks |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=February 1, 2008 |access-date=September 21, 2010}} On April 2, 2008, Crittenton had a career high of 23 points in a 130–114 win over the New York Knicks. === Washington Wizards (2008–2009) === On December 10, 2008, Crittenton was part of a three-team trade that sent him to the [[Washington Wizards]] along with [[Mike James (basketball, born 1975)|Mike James]] from the [[New Orleans Hornets]]. In exchange, the Wizards sent a conditional first-round draft pick to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] and [[Antonio Daniels]] to the Hornets.{{cite web |title=Wizards Acquire Javaris Crittenton and Mike James |url=http://www.nba.com/wizards/news/crittenton_james_081210.html |work=[[NBA.com]] |date=December 10, 2008 |access-date=December 10, 2008}} On December 21, 2009, Crittenton and teammate [[Gilbert Arenas]] were involved in a locker room confrontation involving unloaded guns.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4787825 |title=Report says Washington Wizards Gilbert Arenas and Javaris Crittenton drew guns on each other – ESPN |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=January 2, 2010 |access-date=May 2, 2012}} In a 2010 interview, former Washington Wizards teammate [[Caron Butler]] stated that "you never know, and that's the crazy thing about it" when questioned if there was going to be a trigger pulled in the incident between Crittenton and Arenas. On January 25, 2010, Crittenton pleaded guilty and was given a year of probation on a misdemeanor gun possession charge stemming from this incident.{{cite news |url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2010/writers/michael_mccann/01/25/crittenton.wizards/index.html?cnn=yes&hpt=T2 |work=CNN |title=Crittenton's plea agreement on gun charges could affect Arenas' future |date=January 25, 2010 |access-date=May 6, 2010 |archive-date=June 4, 2011 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110604015339/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2010/writers/michael_mccann/01/25/crittenton.wizards/index.html?cnn=yes&hpt=T2 |url-status=dead }} Two days later, Crittenton and Arenas were suspended for the rest of the season by NBA commissioner [[David Stern]].{{cite web |author=Marc Stein |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=4862783 |title=Stern bans Arenas, Crittenton for year |publisher=[[ESPN]] |date=January 27, 2010 |access-date=May 2, 2012}} He was released by the Wizards following the suspension, while Arenas rejoined the team. === Zhejiang Guangsha Lions (2010) === On September 22, 2010, the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] signed Crittenton to a non-guaranteed contract.{{Cite web |title=Bobcats invite Javaris Crittenton |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=5603128 |access-date=May 19, 2022 |website=ESPN| date=September 22, 2010 }} They released him three weeks later on October 15.{{Cite web |title=Bobcats Release Javaris Crittenton |url=https://www.nba.com/hornets/release_crittenton_101015.html |access-date=May 19, 2022 |website=NBA}} In December 2010, Crittenton played five games for the [[Zhejiang Guangsha Lions]] of the [[Chinese Basketball Association]]. He averaged 25.8 points per game,{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7604689/former-washington-wizard-javaris-crittenton-back-jail |title=Former Washington Wizard Javaris Crittenton back in jail – ESPN |publisher=Espn.go.com |date=February 22, 2012 |access-date=May 2, 2012}} but he returned to the United States after just a few weeks. ===Dakota Wizards (2011)=== In February 2011, Crittenton joined the [[Dakota Wizards]] of the [[NBA Development League|NBA D-League]]. He played 21 games for the minor league team, including five starts. This is the last professional team he played for before later being arrested in 2011 for manslaughter charges. ==Murder and drug charges== {{Infobox criminal | penalty = 23 years in prison
(reduced to 10 years) | conviction = [[Voluntary manslaughter]] with a weapon
Aggravated assault with a firearm | capture_status = Free | victims = Jullian Jones | date = August 19, 2011 | weapons = | imprisoned = }} On August 26, 2011, Crittenton was charged with the August 19 murder of Jullian Jones, a 22-year-old mother of four. [[Atlanta Police Department]] indicated that Jones was not the intended target; they believed that Crittenton was targeting a person who robbed him in April 2011.{{cite web |title=Former NBA player Crittenton charged with murder in Atlanta |url=https://www.tsn.ca/nba/story/?id=374563 |work=[[The Sports Network]] |access-date=August 27, 2011}} Jones was shot in the leg and died during surgery.{{cite web |last=Stevens |first=Alexis |title=Former Georgia Tech star wanted for homicide |url=http://www.ajc.com/news/atlanta/former-georgia-tech-star-1146197.html |work=[[Atlanta Journal-Constitution]] |access-date=August 27, 2011}} Crittenton was arrested by the [[FBI]] at [[John Wayne Airport]] in [[Orange County, California]], on August 29, while waiting to board a flight back to Atlanta. His lawyer stated that Crittenton's sole purpose for the trip to Atlanta was to surrender himself to custody.{{cite news |title=FBI arrests Javaris Crittenton |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/6906139/fbi-arrests-javaris-crittenton-california-airport |agency=Associated Press |publisher=ESPN |access-date=August 30, 2011}} Crittenton was extradited to Atlanta to stand trial for the murder. After his arrest, he denied any involvement.{{cite web |title=Javaris Crittenton back in Atlanta |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/6972466/former-washington-wizards-player-javaris-crittenton-returned-atlanta |work=[[ESPN]] |date=September 15, 2011 |access-date=September 18, 2011}} Crittenton was released on a $230,000 bond.{{cite web |title=Javaris Crittenton free on bond |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/7026631/javaris-crittenton-freed-bond-georgia-murder-case |work=[[ESPN]] |date=September 27, 2011 |access-date=September 27, 2011}} Crittenton and his cousin Douglas Gamble were officially indicted on April 2, 2013, on 12 counts in connection with Jones' death, including charges of murder, felony murder, aggravated assault with a deadly weapon, possession of a firearm during the commission of a felony, giving false statements, attempted murder, and participation in criminal street gang activity. Crittenton reportedly joined the [[Crips]] after signing with the Los Angeles Lakers, according to Fulton County assistant district attorney Gabe Banks, and allegedly also shot at Demontinez Stephens earlier in August 2011.{{cite web |last1=Boyd |first1=Flinder |url=https://www.foxsports.com/stories/other/run-and-gun |title=Run And Gun |work=Fox Sports |date=March 17, 2017 |accessdate=April 5, 2022 |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220224043918/https://www.foxsports.com/stories/other/run-and-gun |archive-date=February 24, 2022}} The target in both shootings was reportedly Trontavious Stephens, Demontinez's brother and a member of the R.O.C. Crew, which is part of the [[Bloods]].{{cite web |last=Garner |first=Marcus K. |title=Ex-Tech star Crittenton indicted for murder |url=http://www.ajc.com/news/news/crime-law/crittenton-indicted-for-murder/nXBDF/ |work=Atlanta Journal-Constitution |access-date=April 3, 2013}} While out on bond on the murder charges, Crittenton was arrested pursuant to a January 10, 2014, indictment of him and 13 other persons who were accused of selling multi-kilo quantities of cocaine and several hundred pounds of marijuana. Crittenton was charged with two counts of conspiracy to violate the Georgia Controlled Substance Act.{{cite web |last=Garner |first=Marcus K. |title=Former NBA player Javaris Crittenton back in jail |url=http://www.ajc.com/news/news/former-nba-star-javaris-crittenton-back-in-jail/ncpTj/ |work=Atlanta Journal-Constitution |access-date=January 15, 2014}} On April 29, 2015, shortly before his trial was set to begin, Crittenton pleaded guilty to voluntary manslaughter with a weapon and aggravated assault with a firearm. He was sentenced to 23 years in prison,{{Cite web |title=Ex-NBA player Crittenton gets 23 years in prison for Atlanta shooting death |date=April 29, 2015 |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/ex-nba-player-crittenton-admits-guilt-2011-shooting-151939187--nba.html |access-date=April 30, 2015}} later reduced to 10 years in a deal with the district attorney. He was released from prison on April 21, 2023.{{Cite web |url=https://www.ajc.com/news/crime/its-not-fair-mother-of-woman-crittenton-killed-unaware-of-sentencing-deal/WMM6DMCABNCRVAAGE23MIYRSCY/ |title='It's not fair': Mother of woman Crittenton killed unaware of sentencing deal |website=The Atlanta Journal-Constitution |date=April 24, 2023}} == NBA career statistics == {{NBA player statistics legend}} === Regular season === {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| {{nbay|2007}} | style="text-align:left;"| [[2007–08 Los Angeles Lakers season|L.A.
